evidence.title: 30-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate
evidence.summary: The snapshotted target change was -0.06 percentage points; it resolved to 'yes'.

evidence.title: September 2024 in Figures – Currency Thoughts
evidence.summary: This source directly states that the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield fell 12 basis points (0.12%) during September, which is a strong indicator for the direction of the 30-year yield, and also notes a 50 basis point Fed rate cut.

evidence.title: August 2024 Market Recap - Pittenger & Anderson, Inc.
evidence.summary: This source indicates a trend of declining Treasury yields in August, with shorter rates falling faster than longer rates, and notes that falling rates boost fixed income returns. This sets a precedent for continued downward pressure on yields into September.

evidence.title: Fed rate-cut size debate follows softening in jobs data | American Banker
evidence.summary: This article discusses the market's reaction to softening jobs data, leading to initial drops in Treasury bond yields and expectations for a Fed rate cut in September. It highlights the debate over the size of the cut (25 vs. 50 bps) but confirms the expectation of a cut.

evidence.title: July PCE reading bolsters outlook for Fed rate cut | National Mortgage News
evidence.summary: This source, published before September, indicates strong market expectations for a Fed rate cut in September, with a significant portion expecting a 50-basis-point cut. This expectation would put downward pressure on Treasury yields.

evidence.title: Government debt yields slip before key US data - BusinessWorld Online
evidence.summary: This article, published at the very beginning of September, confirms that local participants had firmed their expectations of a September US Federal Reserve rate cut following dovish guidance from Fed Chair Jerome H. Powell, leading to a slip in government debt yields.

evidence.title: Jobs report offers no definitive clarity on rate cut size | Bond Buyer
evidence.summary: This source, while noting no definitive clarity on the *size* of the rate cut, still confirms that Treasury bond yields reacted lower to the jobs report and that a rate cut in September was the base case, indicating downward pressure on yields.

evidence.title: Economic Commentary: August 2024 Volatility | Greenleaf Trust
evidence.summary: This commentary provides context on the market's expectation for a September rate cut following Powell's July FOMC meeting remarks and the subsequent reaction to a softer-than-expected jobs report, which caused U.S. government yields to drop precipitously.

evidence.title: U.S. annual inflation in August fell to 2.5%, lowest since February 2021 | Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities
evidence.summary: Lower inflation figures (2.5% in August) would support the Federal Reserve's decision to cut interest rates, as it reduces the pressure to maintain high rates to combat inflation. This would contribute to lower Treasury yields.
